evidence.requirements: All the functional requirements are met. The start page shows title, date and time, 'EUR n per guest' and '<n> seats left' (Home.tsx:30-39, start.jpg). Each tasting has a 'Book <title>' link (Home.tsx:43-45). The form has Name, Email and Guests fields (1-8) and a 'Book' button (BookingPage.tsx:63-72, form.jpg). Seats are enforced on the server (store.ts:38-39), and errors appear next to their field (form.jpg). The confirmation shows the heading 'Booking confirmed', the tasting, guests, total price and reference (confirmation.jpg). /staff has a 'Password' field and 'Sign in' button, checked against STAFF_PASSWORD (app.ts:61-70, index.ts:5). Bookings are grouped by tasting with a Cancel button that frees seats (staff.jpg, store.ts:63-65). There is a fully booked state (Home.tsx:36,42) and the layout is responsive. Partly met: the Process requirement asks for the spec tool, but openspec/specs holds only .gitkeep, so there is no evidence of specs or plans. Phone usability is only implied by sm: classes; there is no mobile screenshot.
evidence.correctness: Seat checking and inserting happen synchronously with no await between them, so concurrent requests cannot overbook (store.ts:34-41), and a test covers this (app.test.ts:106). Boundaries are handled: exactly the seats left, one too many, 0, 9, 2.5, '-1', '', and non-numeric guests (booking.ts:10-13, app.test.ts:53-104). Cancelling deletes the booking, so its seats are counted free again (store.ts:16-20). A 409 refreshes the seat count (BookingPage.tsx:53). References are unique (store.ts:22-27). One flaw: on /staff, any failed load (a 500 or a network error) is treated as signed out and shows the sign-in form instead of an error (Staff.tsx:10-11,16).
evidence.security: React escapes all output. The password check hashes both sides and compares them with timingSafeEqual, and an empty or unset password never matches (app.ts:63-64). The session token is random (randomBytes(24)), expires server-side and is cleared on logout. The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, which protects the DELETE from CSRF. helmet is used, the JSON body limit is 10kb, login is rate-limited, and the error handler does not leak details (app.ts:88-92). No secrets are in the code. Gaps: the cookie has no Secure flag (app.ts:69), and booking has no rate limit, so a script can fill every tasting with fake bookings.
evidence.code_quality: The structure is small and clear: server/app, store and shared schema; the client has pages, a ui.tsx with Field and Notice, and an api helper. One zod schema is shared by client and server (shared/booking.ts). Naming is good and errors are handled consistently. Minuses: some very long one-line JSX early returns (BookingPage.tsx:19,21), type escapes such as `zodResolver(...) as never` (BookingPage.tsx:41) and `as unknown as` casts (Staff.tsx:11, useTastings.ts:11), and a few dense lines (app.ts:85).
evidence.tests: The supertest API tests cover listing, confirmation total and reference, distinct references, 11 invalid-input cases mapped to their field, exact-seat boundaries, fully booked, concurrency, staff authentication (wrong password, forged cookie, unset password), grouping, cancel freeing seats, logout, and cookie flags (app.test.ts). The UI tests with a stubbed fetch cover the start page, fully booked, the load error, field errors with accessible descriptions, the server 409 error, confirmation, staff sign-in and cancel (App.test.tsx). There is no end-to-end test against the built app, and the concurrency test is in-process only.
evidence.ux_design: The look is coherent: wine, cream and olive palette with a serif heading font (start.jpg). The cards are clear with a prominent CTA. The invalid field is highlighted in red with a warning icon and message (form.jpg). The confirmation is a distinct green success panel (confirmation.jpg). There is a fully booked badge and the CTA is hidden for full tastings. The design is plain, with no imagery or winery atmosphere beyond colour and type. Staff cancel has no confirmation step and shows no success feedback.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are tied to inputs via useId. Errors and hints are linked with aria-describedby and aria-invalid (ui.tsx:15-27), and tests check them. Notices use role=alert or status. :focus-visible has an outline. html lang is 'en'. Buttons are at least 44px tall. Cancel buttons are linked to the guest name with aria-describedby (Staff.tsx:74). Muted text has good contrast. Gaps: the page title never changes, focus is not managed when the route changes or the confirmation appears, and field errors returned by the server are not focused or announced.
evidence.simplicity: There are about 600 lines across a handful of files. Dependencies are established and fit the problem: Express, React Router, react-hook-form with zod, and Tailwind. helmet and express-rate-limit are small and justified. There is no server build step (Node type stripping) and no needless abstraction.
evidence.maintainability: The README covers install, build, start, STAFF_PASSWORD, in-memory storage, test, typecheck and dev, and where the tastings are defined. package-lock.json is present, engines asks for node >=22.18, and the tests plus typecheck give regression coverage. Missing: there is no CI pipeline, no ADRs, docs or specs (openspec/specs is empty), no staff manual, no changelog or release approach, and no .nvmrc. The Node 22.18+ type-stripping requirement is not stated in the README.
evidence.visual_design: Typography, colour and spacing are consistent across all four screenshots. The header has a wine-coloured bottom rule, cards have soft shadows, and badges are pill-shaped. It looks finished and coherent but generic, with no logo or imagery. On staff.jpg the date line inside the h2 uses the serif font while the rest of the meta text is sans, a small inconsistency.
evidence.layout: The hierarchy is clear: header, intro, then tasting cards with the CTA on the right (start.jpg). The form and confirmation are capped at max-w-xl, which leaves a large empty area on the right on desktop (form.jpg, confirmation.jpg). Staff bookings are grouped into sections with dividers (staff.jpg). Nothing overlaps or is clipped.
evidence.usability: A guest books in two steps with clear labels. The seats-left hint sits under Guests, Guests defaults to 2, and there are back links (form.jpg). Errors show inline and the confirmation is clear. Staff sign in and cancel quickly. However, Cancel acts immediately with no confirmation, so a misclick loses a booking. Staff also get no notice that a cancel succeeded.
evidence.reception: Guests would find it trustworthy and on-brand for a small family winery. The tone is warm ('Come to the cellar...', confirmation.jpg) and it looks professional. It would feel more like the winery's own site with imagery or a short description of each tasting.

unmet_requirements: Process: no evidence the spec tool was used (openspec/specs contains only .gitkeep)
Usable on a phone: responsive classes exist, but it was not verified with a mobile screenshot or test
strengths: Correct, race-free seat logic with one zod schema shared by client and server, and thorough boundary validation shown next to each field
Careful staff security: hashed timingSafeEqual check, password never matches when unset, random server-side sessions, HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, login rate limit, helmet
Meaningful API and UI tests that map closely to the brief, plus a coherent, polished winery visual style
issues: Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, no specs, ADRs or staff manual (openspec/specs is empty), no release or changelog approach, and the Node 22.18+ type-stripping requirement is not in the README
Staff Cancel deletes immediately with no confirmation or success feedback, and a failed staff load is shown as the sign-in form (Staff.tsx:10-16)
No rate limit on booking and no Secure flag on the session cookie; the page title never changes and focus is not managed on route change or confirmation
review.verdict: This is a compact, correct and secure booking app that meets every functional requirement of the brief and looks like a coherent winery site. It could ship once it has a CI pipeline and some docs or specs, and staff get a cancel confirmation; none of these block a small winery launch.
